correctness.rationale: Let a=p−1. Expanding a proper r-minor of aI+J by columns uses at most one J-column in any nonzero term and gives divisibility by a^(r−1). Taking rows 0,…,r−1 and columns 1,…,r and subtracting the unmatched row realizes exactly ±a^(r−1), including r=1. The full determinant is a^(p−1)(a+p), so the consecutive determinantal-divisor ratios are precisely the claimed local multiset, including {1,3} at p=2. CRT factors the numerical gcd of the difference for squarefree N, making the matrix the Kronecker product after reindexing. Both tensor products of the local Smith transformations are unimodular by tensoring their integral inverses. Thus the product entries form an integer diagonal presentation; sorting valuations separately and aligning equal positions is the structure theorem over each prime and then CRT, not a sort of the unsplit integer entries. The determinant formula also follows from the positive prime-factor determinants and the tensor determinant identity. For modulo ell, if a vanishes the local matrix is J, of rank one; otherwise a times the identity plus a rank-one perturbation has kernel at most one-dimensional, and its determinant vanishes exactly if ell divides 2p−1. This includes ell=p without any eigenspace decomposition assumption. Tensor ranks multiply. The generator number is the maximum dimension of the cokernel modulo a prime. The minimum total rank is one at ell=2 for odd N, and at most two for even N by ell=2. For even N rank one forces ell=3 by the factor at p=2, and every odd local factor then has rank one exactly for p≡1 mod 3. Otherwise ell=3 has a factor of rank at least three, and ell=2 is a minimizer. N=2 is the separate one-generator case. This proves the all-N statements directly without extrapolating numerical samples.
residual_risks: The analytic proof concerns squarefree N; recorded determinant/minor checks and optional Smith replays are examples only. No extension to arbitrary prime powers is inferred.

value.rationale: The numerical GCD difference kernel is a natural arithmetic convolution on a cyclic group. The output gives its complete finite integral cokernel uniformly, retaining mixed-prime information not supplied by a determinant or rational spectrum. In particular the exact generator count distinguishes even squarefree orders according to the residues of all their odd prime factors modulo three. This arithmetic distinction and the complete family prescription are the useful content; the local rank-one Smith calculation alone is routine.
residual_risks: This is specialized to a numerical GCD kernel, not a general Smith algorithm for circulants and not a classification at arbitrary N.
